title: ISO/IEC 42001:2023 to the EU AI Act (amended)

useCase.intendedUsers: Lead auditors and reviewers on engagements that use either framework as criteria.
useCase.purpose: Show where ISO/IEC 42001 audit evidence also bears on AI Act obligations, and where it does not.
useCase.assumptions: Relationships compare what each requirement demands, not how an organisation implements it. No inference may be drawn from requirements that are not mapped. Every entry is a draft until the clause numbers are confirmed against licensed copies (#57).

entries.justification: Both require an established risk process. ISO/IEC 42001 addresses risks to the organisation's AI objectives; Art. 9(1) requires a lifecycle risk-management system for one high-risk system. Neither contains the other.
Performing assessments at planned intervals supports the 'maintained' element of Art. 9(1) but does not establish the system-level risk-management system.
An established management system overlaps with the quality management system of Art. 17, which lists provider-specific elements the standard does not require.
Technical documentation of an AI system overlaps with Art. 11(1), whose content is fixed by Annex IV and goes further.
Event logging overlaps with the record-keeping duties of Art. 12, which set specific logging capabilities.
Data controls overlap with the data governance duties of Art. 10, which add quality criteria for training, validation and testing data.
Information for users overlaps with the instructions for use of Art. 13, whose content is prescribed.
An impact assessment overlaps with the fundamental rights impact assessment of Art. 27, which applies to certain deployers and has prescribed content.
Monitoring and measurement overlap with post-market monitoring under Art. 72, which requires a plan and data collection from the market.
Communicating incidents overlaps with serious-incident reporting under Art. 73, which sets recipients and deadlines.
